item.title: Attempted attack with explosives in New York City investigated as "ISIS-inspired terrorism"
item.summary: Two men have been charged with allegedly providing support to a foreign terrorism organization and using a weapon of mass destruction. New York City NYPD Commissioner says the explosive devices "could have caused serious injury or death."

item.title: Top Arizona lawmaker says he's complied with a subpoena for 2020 election records
item.summary: Arizona's state Senate president says he has complied with a subpoena he received last week seeking records from a flawed, Republican-led review of the 2020 election in Maricopa County.

item.title: What to know about Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's new supreme leader
item.summary: The second son of the late supreme leader keeps a low profile. But he's long been viewed as wielding his power behind the scenes, from crushing dissent to influencing presidential elections.

item.title: Anthropic sues the Trump administration over 'supply chain risk' label
item.summary: The Pentagon told suppliers they can't use Anthropic's artificial intelligence tools after the company said it would not let its tech be used for autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance.

item.title: Americana's newcomer Jobi Riccio faces the pressure on her new record
item.summary: The country and bluegrass songwriter talks about her sophomore album, Face the Feeling, out May 15.

item.title: Trump is using immigration policy to suppress speech, lawsuit claims
item.summary: A new lawsuit accuses the administration of violating the First Amendment by threatening the visas of researchers for work on disinformation and content moderation of social media.

item.title: Why young girls are disguised as boys in Afghanistan
item.summary: The Taliban has released a video of an interrogation of a girl who passed as a boy. It's an age-old practice in this patriarchal society but now appears to be happening with some frequency.

item.title: Bill Kurtis retires as 'Wait Wait...Don't Tell Me!' judge and scorekeeper
item.summary: Legendary anchorman and America's favorite judge and scorekeeper, Bill Kurtis is retiring from his role at Wait Wait…Don't Tell Me!, capping off a phenomenal 12-year run with the show.

item.title: Epstein used his ties to Nobel laureate scientists to try to rebuild his image
item.summary: A 2006 conference for physicists in the U.S. Virgin Islands that included a trip to Jeffrey Epstein's private island shows how he used his wealth to build relationships with prominent scientists.

item.title: This historian dug up the hidden history of 'amateur' blackface in America
item.summary: In her new book, Darkology, historian Rhae Lynn Barnes writes about how blackface and minstrel shows became one of the most popular forms of entertainment in 19th- and 20th-century America.
